q: What is the carbon footprint of rock wool insulation per kg?
title: Rock wool insulation CO2 per kg
short: Rock wool is made by melting basalt and slag, often in a coke fired cupola, then spinning fibres and curing a binder. Coke combustion is the main CO2; carbonate fluxes add process CO2. Divide by kg of finished product.
audience: Insulation makers, builders and HVAC contractors

ul: Scope 1: coke or gas in the melter, curing oven fuel.
Process CO2 from any limestone or dolomite in the charge.
Scope 3: binder, packaging, slag bought in.

p: An electric melter moves most of the CO2 into Scope 2 and cuts it if the power is renewable.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
